name: Azelaoyl diglycinate

card.summary: A water-soluble derivative of azelaic acid, used in skincare to calm redness and target acne-prone, blotchy skin.
card.note: Studies are small; cosmetic ingredient rather than approved drug.

quick.overview:
Azelaoyl diglycinate (potassium azeloyl diglycinate, azeloglycine) is a derivative of azelaic acid that dissolves in water, making it easier to formulate into light creams and serums. It appears in products for acne-prone, red or uneven skin.

Azelaic acid itself treats acne, rosacea and hyperpigmentation by reducing inflammation and melanin production; the derivative is studied for similar soothing effects.
quick.how: It is applied topically in creams or gels, usually twice daily in studies, often with other soothing ingredients such as nicotinamide or hydroxypropyl chitosan. A rosacea study used a cream with 5 percent of it for 12 weeks.
quick.risks: The rosacea study reported no side effects. Azelaic acid itself can cause dryness and irritation. Research on the derivative is limited.

lead: Azelaoyl diglycinate is a derivative of azelaic acid joined to two glycine units, sold as potassium azeloyl diglycinate or azeloglycine in cosmetic products. [1][2]

Azelaic acid is used for acne, rosacea and pigmentation. Topical 15 to 20 percent azelaic acid treats mild to moderate acne and can lighten melasma and post-inflammatory marks by inhibiting tyrosinase, with dryness and irritation as the main side effects. [5]

The derivative has been studied for formulation advantages and for soothing action: it improved hydrogel rheology and tetracycline stability in lab work, down-regulated pro-inflammatory mediators in vitro with nicotinamide, and reduced stinging and burning in rosacea patients. [1][2][3][4]

chain: Applied in a topical cream or gel
Less redness, calmer and clearer-looking skin
angle.text: It is applied to acne-prone, red or sensitive skin to reduce irritation and visible inflammation, with azelaic-acid-type benefits for clarity and tone.

paras: It combines azelaic acid with glycine, improving water solubility in formulations. Hydrogel studies found it improved rheological properties and reduced tetracycline degradation under alkaline conditions. [1][2]

Azelaic acid reduces comedones, papules and pustules, with benefits visible from about 4 weeks, and treats melasma and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation. The derivative is aimed at similar acne-prone and uneven skin. [5]

In an open multicentre study, 37 adults with erythemato-telangiectatic rosacea used a cream with 5 percent potassium azeloyl diglycinate and 1 percent hydroxypropyl chitosan twice daily for 12 weeks. Stinging and burning scores fell 56.1 percent and no side effects were reported. [3] A lab study found azeloglycine with nicotinamide down-regulated pro-inflammatory mediators. [4]
